- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope after peak.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.4) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates continuation; cap forecast growth at 3–5% above recent 7-day moving average.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.1–0.4), model exhibits lagged response; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment momentum.
- Mean reversion is overemphasized in model — if price is >+10% above 30-day mean, reduce forecast by 2–4% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period volatility; add 1–2% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment is rising or neutral.
